objective: Apply ordered ASIL-decomposition, hardware-metrics, and V&V completion gates to five ADAS functions and record the first failing check for each release review.

items.rationale: The decomposition verifier accepted FN-AEB, reporting decomposition_valid=true, child rank sum 5 against parent rank 4, four independence claims, and a DFA reference. The hardware engine accepted the supplied metrics against programme targets: PMHF 6.2 FIT <= 10 FIT, SPFM 99.4% >= 99%, and LFM 92.1% >= 90%. The V&V report accepted 97.4% coverage with 0 open defects, so this is a DRAFT release candidate pending safety-manager review, not proof of safety.

gates.name: ASIL Decomposition
gates.detail: FN-AEB, FN-ACC, FN-TJA, and FN-APA were accepted; FN-LKA was rejected because child rank sum 3 does not cover parent rank 4. The gate therefore does not pass across the release set.

gates.name: PMHF / hardware metrics
gates.detail: The fmea_fta_engine calls returned programme targets PMHF <=10 FIT, SPFM >=99%, and LFM >=90% for every function, including the ASIL-C and ASIL-B calls. FN-TJA failed SPFM at 98.9%; the other supplied hardware summaries passed.

gates.name: V&V
gates.detail: FN-AEB, FN-LKA, FN-ACC, and FN-TJA returned vv_complete=true with DRAFT reports; FN-APA errored on 1 open defect, so completion was rejected. For FN-LKA and FN-TJA the V&V results remain informational after earlier failures.

gates.name: HARA
gates.detail: Not assessed: no HARA input or brief rule was supplied, and hara_automate was not called.

gates.name: Safety Concept
gates.detail: Not assessed by this brief or plan; the V&V tool's gate_snapshot.safety_concept_approved=false does not amount to a safety-concept review.

gates.name: Release
gates.detail: Not passed or assessed: all positive item outcomes remain DRAFT candidates requiring safety-manager review and release-board disposition.

overall_verdict: FN-AEB and FN-ACC are DRAFT release candidates pending safety-manager review, while FN-LKA fails decomposition, FN-TJA fails hardware metrics, and FN-APA has incomplete V&V; this gate review does not establish that any function is safe or authorize release.
limitations: All inputs are synthetic teaching-scenario records, so this is a mechanical gate assessment rather than a real-programme safety determination.
DFA completion and independence claims were taken from input text; asil_decompose_verify only counted claims and detected DFA references, without verifying independence or freedom from interference.

FMEDA values are supplied summaries, not independently re-derived results, because the inputs contain no failure_modes or lifetime_h; fmea_fta_engine returned source=supplied_summary and its own modelling limitations.
V&V evidence content was counted rather than verified, and illustrative vv_report_path files were not opened or checked for existence.

FN-ACC was assessed with programme-wide ASIL-D targets despite its ASIL-C ISO targets of PMHF <100 FIT, SPFM >=97%, and LFM >=80%; FN-APA was assessed with those same ASIL-D targets despite its ASIL-B ISO targets of PMHF <100 FIT, SPFM >=90%, and LFM >=60%. This brief-directed, more stringent choice should be confirmed by the safety manager.

CAPABILITIES.md notes a strict README PMHF threshold of <10 FIT, while the applied programme rule returned and used PMHF <=10 FIT; no measured PMHF equalled the boundary, so this notation difference changed no outcome.
FN-APA also has safety_case.open_goals=1, but that field was reported only as a flag because the brief's V&V gate uses requirements coverage and open defects.
HARA, Safety Concept, and Release gates were not assessed; passing the three assessed checks does not authorize release or prove safety.

The requested top-level JSON shape has no separate raw-evidence object, so tool outputs are recorded as key-value evidence strings within each item rather than under PLAN.md's proposed evidence.<tool>.<function> hierarchy.
